MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 12, 2019

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Raths at 5:00 p.m., on March 12, 2019, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on March 7, 2019, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Goodell
  Mayor Raths

Absent:  None

Staff Present: Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Labor Negotiations - The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957 and 54957.6. The Parties to the
  Negotiations Are the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s
  Negotiator is Dennis Wilberg.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Raths recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  March 12, 2019
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council heard information regarding labor relations
and provided direction to staff but no reportable actions occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Boy Scout Troop 603

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Cathy Allen on her Retirement from the Mission Viejo Activities
  Committee

  Mayor Raths presented the proclamation to Cathy Allen.

P2.  Featured Businesses of the Month - 21-13 Impact Graphics, Inc., and The Right Hair Salon

  Mayor Raths presented proclamations to business owners Jan Miller and Brandee Pacillio.

P3.  Key to the City - Jeff Zaret

  Mayor Raths presented Jeff Zaret with a Key to the City.

P4.  Recognize Girl Scout Francesca Dreyer

  Mayor Raths presented the certificate of appreciation to Francesca Dreyer.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Ron Yee, Chairman of the Mission Viejo Community of Character Committee, M.V.: shared traits
that define integrity which is the Community of Character word for the month of March.

Mary Harris, M.V.: thanked the Mayor and City Attorney for working hard to help residents of the
Mosaic Apartments who were being threatened with eviction from their Section 8 low income
housing.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 9 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None
City Council Minutes  2  March 12, 2019
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of February 26, 2019, as
  presented.

2.  Check Register Dated February 15, 2019 in the Amount of $1,013,066.75

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated February 22, 2019 in the Amount of $2,100,603.96

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Disbursement of Donations Received for School Safety

  Approved distribution of funds on deposit for school safety improvements to CUSD of
  $15,453 and SVUSD of $28,698 for school safety purposes.

5.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2019

  Received and filed.

6.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January 2019

  Received and filed.

7.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for January 2019

  Received and filed.

8.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for January
  2019

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

9.  Sale of Vacant Remainder Parcels to Mountain Star Development, Inc.

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Goodell, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to (1)
  authorize the City Manager to sell the vacant city-owned remainder parcels known as
  Parcel Numbers 375.4, Z21-375.21, and 376.3 on El Toro Road to Mountain Star
  Development, Inc., for $16,500; and (2) authorize the City Manager to execute all
  documents required to complete the sale.

City Council Minutes  3  March 12, 2019
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

10.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  Council Member Sachs presented the report.

11.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Council Member Kelley presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

12.  Mid-Year Budget Review for FY 2018-19

  Administrative Services Manager Susan Knudson presented the staff report and Director
  of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas answered the Council Members questions.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to
  adopt Resolution 19-04 Amending the FY 2018-19 Budget for Adjustments to Certain
  Revenue Sources and Operating and Capital Improvement Program Appropriations.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  Mission Viejo Shuttle Status

  Director of Public Works Mark Chagnon announced that the City received a Notice of
  Cancelation for the MV Shuttle from Orange County Transportation Authority (OCTA)
  due to low ridership. Mr. Chagnon noted that City staff submitted a letter to OCTA
  opposing the cancelation but OCTA staff dismissed the City’s issues.

  By consensus, the Council directed staff to continue working to try and maintain the MV
  Shuttle service.

14.  Routine Bidding of Maintenance Contracts - Review and submittal of Schedule

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

City Council Minutes  4  March 12, 2019
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

15.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum thanked Council Member Kelley for attending the recent Southern
California Association of Governments (SCAG) meeting and giving tonight’s report. She outlined
her attendance at the Orange County Board of Supervisors Meeting earlier today where the Orange
County Housing Trust was approved. Council Member Bucknum said she was involved in the
effort to establish the Housing Trust with the Association of California Cities-Orange County, in
an effort to bring Sacramento dollars back to cities for things like workforce housing. She
announced that the Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce hosted a new event last night, a happy
hour at Union Market in Kaleidoscope shopping center. She said it was very well attended and she
thanked the Chamber for trying something new. Council Member Bucknum outlined upcoming
events including a pancake breakfast fundraiser on Sunday, March 17, to support Deputy Carolynn
Cuzynski’s participation in the Police Unity Tour in memory of Sergeant Matt Davis. The
breakfast will be held at Los Aliso Intermediate School from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. The Mission
Viejo Activities Committee will also host the 2nd annual Irish Fest from 11:00 a.m. to 3:00 p.m.
on Saturday, March 16.

Council Member Bucknum had a prior commitment and departed the meeting at 7:46 p.m.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley stated that she was pleased to be Principal for day at Castille Elementary
School on March 1. She commended Principal Laura Lyon and said that she was very impressed
with the school. She was also a guest at Cordillera Elementary School’s Pacific Symphony Class
Act program and she noted that she has shared information on the great music program with other
schools for consideration. Council Member Kelley outlined her attendance at additional meetings
including a Government Leaders Prayer Breakfast and a meeting with the Superintendent of
Capistrano Unified School District (CUSD) on a future bond measure that the district will be
considering that will be specific to each city. She shared that CUSD will begin offering music
instruction from kindergarten through third grade and both school districts will be starting all day
kindergarten next year. Council Member Kelley further discussed the new sex education program
that is coming to schools and noted that some of the content is state mandated but she credited
CUSD for developing their own curriculum that matches more closely with the community. She
reminded parents that they can opt out of the entire program or specific lessons that they find
objectionable. The program begins in May and information is available on the CUSD website.
Council Member Kelley warned parents of a potential Instagram scam that some local teenagers
were involved in and she encouraged parents to be extra vigilant. She thanked City Clerk Karen
Hamman for the 2018 Annual Report which, she said, has a wealth of good information. Council
Member Kelley concluded her comments with a reminder that the character word for the month of
March is integrity and the character film is Mr. Holland's Opus, showing at 2:00 p.m. on Sunday,
March 17. She shared a quote from Warren Buffet: “In looking for people to hire, you look for
City Council Minutes  5  March 12, 2019
 three qualities: integrity, intelligence, and energy. And if you don’t have the first, the other two
will kill you” and a quote from Horton the elephant in the book Horton Hatches the Egg: “I meant
what I said and I said what I meant. An elephant's faithful one-hundred percent!”

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs announced that he had nothing to report.

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell

Mayor Pro Tem Goodell discussed his attendance at the Government Leaders Prayer Breakfast
and a meeting with Capistrano Unified School District Superintendent Vitale to discuss the
proposed community-specific bond measures. He announced that he’ll be heading to Sacramento
next week with the Association of California Cities-Orange County on a legislative advocacy trip.
Mayor Pro Tem Goodell shared that the Olympic Promotion Committee is working with a
consultant that has extensive experience with the Olympics and they are picking his brain for ideas
for promoting Mission Viejo for Olympic events. He reminded residents that the Fina Diving
Grand Prix will be held at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex from April 11-14, 2019, with world
class Olympic-level divers coming from all over the globe to participate. He also announced that
the Nadadores have secured another major event, the first ever United States Professional
Swimming League competition. Mayor Pro Tem Goodell discussed the possibility of dirt for lower
Curtis park and noted that the geotechnical work was delayed due to the rains. He said the hope is
to make some more park space in the community.

Mayor Raths

Mayor Raths announced that he will talk with Orange County Transportation Authority Board
Members about the MV Shuttle and he will work with the City Manager and City Attorney to
make sure the City doesn’t lose the service. He discussed his attendance at a tri-city Chamber
mixer with Rancho Santa Margarita and Lake Forest at Arroyo Trabuco Golf Course. He thanked
the Mission Viejo Chamber for working with the other chambers to make it happen. Mayor Raths
discussed his participation as Principal for a Day at Capistrano Valley High School and said he
was blown away by the kids’ talents. He noted that he also attended a good meeting of the Southern
California Association of Governments Environmental and Energy Committee and Chapman
University’s 20th annual Holocaust art and writing contest. Mayor Raths congratulated Trabuco
Hills High School students for entering the contest and doing so well.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:04 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Raths adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, March 26, 2019, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 26, 2019

City Council Minutes  6  March 12, 2019
